Subject: QBR prep: AveryTech health check & renewal risk register

Hi all,

We have AveryTech's QBR the week of May 10th. I wanted to pull together a concise health snapshot + an updated renewal risk register for the exec readout. Sara — thanks in advance for any quick updates you can share on usage/ROI items below.

Ask for internal team (Lauren/Marissa/Grace/Neha):
- Can you each review the attached draft risk register and add one-line mitigations for any red/amber items by EOD Friday? (attached: avery_qbr_draft_risk_register.xlsx)
- Please flag any gaps in logs/metrics we should surface to the customer during the QBR (latency spikes, token-cost regressions, billing disputes).
- Recommend 1-2 escalation asks for exec attention (credits/credits+SLA changes/strategic resource assignment).

Sara — quick questions for your QBR slide:
- Current monthly token consumption vs. last quarter (approx)
- Any new security/compliance requests since our last call
- Renewal timeline & procurement path (names/contacts)

I'll consolidate into a 1-page exec highlight and circulate to the leadership thread Monday.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Head of Growth, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
Attachments: avery_qbr_draft_risk_register.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@averytech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-28T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: AveryTech health check & renewal risk register

Hi Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the draft. Quick answers so your team can start:

- Consumption: We've grown ~18% QoQ. March run-rate was ~1.2B tokens/month (up from 1.02B in Dec).
- ROI/Usage: We're using embeddings for search expansion (largest driver) and inference for customer support automation (smaller). Latency tolerances have been OK but we saw two latency incidents in March tied to a model rollback.
- Security: No new SOC requests, but InfoSec has asked for an updated data retention map (I can share a short note).
- Procurement: Renewal target date is 2027-06-21. Primary procurement contact is procurement@averytech.com; legal will be involved for a PO.

We can share a short usage export if that helps.

Sara
Sara Liu
Director, Product Operations — AveryTech
sara.liu@averytech.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: AveryTech health check & renewal risk register

Thanks Jordan — I reviewed the draft and updated the register with three priority risks and proposed mitigations (see attached). High-level summary for execs below. Attachment: renewal_playbook_notes.pdf

Top 3 risks (impact / mitigation / ask)
1) Renewal timeline compression (High) — procurement wants sign-off by 2027-06-21. Mitigation: propose a two-week commercial review window + pre-signed amendment template. Ask: Exec approval for a one-time 6% renewal credit if needed to close by target date.
2) Latency incident recurrence (Medium) — March rollback shows model-variant fragility. Mitigation: schedule a dedicated reliability runbook + prod canary window and increase tracing retention for last-mile latency. Ask: Engineering to allocate one SRE sprint (2 FTE-weeks) during May.
3) Cost/regression surprise (Medium) — token consumption growth could trigger unexpected overages. Mitigation: recommend a cost guardrail (token-cap triggers + mid-month alerts) and a suggested quantization/variant move for non-critical endpoints. Ask: CS to propose a billing-prorate plan for predictable thresholds.

Additional notes: Sara indicated InfoSec wants a data retention map. Grace — can you take point on that and attach a short note? Neha — please confirm whether we can offer the pre-signed amendment template (legal) and I can route to procurement.

Lauren Bishop
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Exec attention: AveryTech renewal risk + QBR highlight (short)

FYI — consolidating for the exec thread ahead of the QBR (May 10th). Below are the top-line items that need leadership attention and an ask for fast decisions: please review and reply if you have objections.

Snapshot:
- Customer: AveryTech (DEAL-AVT-3492) — renewal target 2027-06-21
- Health: Usage up 18% QoQ; main value from embeddings for search. Two latency incidents noted (March) after a model rollback — no security escalations yet.

Leadership asks (decision needed):
1) One-time renewal credit (up to 6%) to preserve timeline and prevent procurement churn. This is a commercial lever to close by 6/21.
2) Approve allocation of one SRE sprint (2 FTE-weeks) in May to reduce latency risk and add canary coverage.
3) Approve pre-signed amendment template to accelerate procurement/legal sign-off (Neha, can you confirm availability?).

Supporting artifacts (attached/linked):
- avery_qbr_draft_risk_register.xlsx (links to prioritized items)
- renewal_playbook_notes.pdf
- HubSpot: HS-523441
- DocuSign: https://docusign.net/averytech-renewal-3492

If leadership approves the three asks above, CS will: finalize slide, signal procurement/legal, and offer the amendment during the QBR.
